question: A toroid has $600$ turns and carries a current of $3\text{ A}$. Find the magnetic field at a point inside the core where the mean radius is $0.20\text{ m}$. Also state why the magnetic field outside an ideal toroid is nearly zero. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$.

options.A: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2\pi r}=9.0\times10^{-4}\,\text{T}$; the field outside is non-zero because the toroid encloses current.
options.B: $B=\dfrac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})(600)(3)}{2\pi(0.20)}=1.8\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$. Outside an ideal toroid, the field is nearly zero because an Amperian loop outside encloses zero net current.
options.C: $B=3.6\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$; the field outside is uniform and equals the field inside.
options.D: $B=1.8\times10^{-4}\,\text{T}$; the field outside is zero because a toroid carries no current.
